reasoning: Spot identification: hero HJ with AsJs on Jc8d4h rainbow flop in 3-bet pot. Preflop: UTG opens 2.5bb, hero(HJ) flats, CO 3-bets to 11bb, UTG calls, hero calls; 3-way at decision with UTG cold-caller and CO 3-bettor remaining. Hero is sandwiched between UTG (acts first) and CO (acts last, was preflop aggressor). UTG has checked; action is on hero, facing_bet=0. Pot 34bb, SPR roughly 2.6. Per-villain range chains: UTG cold-called a 3-bet from out of position, which is the most range-capped action in poker — eliminates AA/KK/QQ/AK (all 4-bet preferred), leaves JJ-99, AQs, sometimes 87s/T9s suited connectors that flop well in 3-bet pots; on J-8-4 UTG continues with JJ overpair (hero blocks one combo with the Js+Jh dead), set-8, set-4 (rare), TT-99 underpair-floats, AQ overcards. CO 3-bettor's range from CO vs HJ-flat is QQ+/AKs/AKo plus light suited blockers (A5s-A4s, KQs); on J-8-4 CO's value continues are QQ+/AKs with overcards plus backdoors — KK and AA c-bet near 100% in this geometry, QQ mixes, AK c-bets a balanced frequency with overcards. Equity tensions: hero AsJs is top pair top kicker with backdoor nut flush draw and backdoor wheel/broadway — strong but not nut. Vs UTG's capped range hero is ahead of TT-99/AQ but behind set-J/set-8; vs CO's polar range hero is crushed by QQ+ and flips/ahead of AK. 3-way equity realization ~0.85; the realization tax matters because hero is OOP to CO. Spot factors: hero is middle position OOP to the preflop aggressor sitting behind — donk-leading announces a polar value-or-protection range and surrenders the betting initiative that GTO assigns to the 3-bettor. CO's range bets J-high boards in 3-bet pots at high frequency; checking lets CO c-bet the entire polar range including bluffs and overcard hands hero dominates, while UTG's capped range stays defined. Hero blocks AJ/JJ which mildly weakens CO's value but the structural argument dominates: in 3-bet pots the cold-caller checks to the 3-bettor with strong-but-non-nut TPTK because raising the eventual c-bet folds out bluffs and isolates value. Decision: CHECK with plan to check-call CO's c-bet up to ~66% sizing. Adjacent alternatives: BET 33% is defensible to deny equity vs UTG's AQ overcards and protect vs runner-runner draws, but it sacrifices the higher-EV check-call line that preserves CO's bluff frequency in the pot and avoids being raised off equity by CO's overpairs.

Spot identification: hero UTG with AhJs on QhJh3s two-tone flop in 4-way 3-bet pot. Preflop: UTG(hero) opens 2.5bb, CO 3-bets 9bb, BTN calls, SB calls, hero(UTG) calls; 3 opponents remaining at decision (CO 3-bettor, BTN cold-caller IP, SB cold-caller OOP). Hero is OOP-earliest with all 3 villains behind. Pot 36bb, SPR ~1.78. facing_bet=0; action is on hero first to act. Per-villain range chains: CO 3-bettor squeezing vs UTG-open from CO position has range QQ+/AK plus some suited bluff blockers (KQs, A5s); on QhJh3s CO crushes with QQ (set, hero blocks 0 combos), AA/KK overpairs, AK with nut-FD potential (AhKh blocked by hero's Ah), JJ for set (hero blocks). BTN cold-call of a squeeze IP is a very strong range action — JJ-TT, AQs-AJs, KQs, suited connectors 89s-T9s that flop straight equity; on Q-J-3 BTN has set-J, TT, JJ (hero blocks), AQ, KhTh/KhQh FD combos, T9s gutter. SB cold-calling a 3-bet OOP is the tightest action of all — TT-JJ, AQs, KQs only; on this board SB has AQ, KQs, occasional set. Equity tensions: hero has middle-pair-top-kicker with a gutshot to KT broadway and one heart (Ah) blocker but no flush draw. Vs CO's range hero is dominated by overpairs and set-Q; flips vs AK; ahead of bluff-blockers. Vs BTN+SB combined ranges hero is behind most continuing combos because they didn't peel air. 4-way equity realization ~0.75 — hero's pair realizes poorly OOP-earliest. Spot factors: this is the maximum-pressure seat in poker — OOP to three villains in a 3-bet pot on a wet two-tone board where the 3-bettor's range range-bets and the IP cold-callers have continuation incentives. Donk-leading announces a polar capped range that CO can raise (set-Q, overpairs) and IP villains can flat with equity; hero cannot win the pot multiway with a single bet on Q-J-3 with middle pair. Standard 4-way 3-bet-pot OOP-earliest structure: check to the 3-bettor, let CO c-bet polar, fold to subsequent multiway action or check-call a single c-bet given pair+gutter. Decision: CHECK with intent to check-call a normal-sized CO c-bet (25-33%) and re-evaluate on turn. Adjacent alternatives: BET 25% is dominated because it gets raised by IP value, isolates hero OOP vs better, and forfeits the structural lead CO is supposed to take in 3-bet pots.

Spot identification: hero BTN with AcJs on Jh7d2s rainbow flop in 3-bet pot. Preflop: UTG opens 2.5bb, CO 3-bets 9bb, hero(BTN) cold-calls, SB+BB fold, UTG calls; 2 opponents at decision (UTG cold-caller, CO 3-bettor). UTG checked, CO bet 7bb into 20bb (~35% c-bet); facing_bet=1, to_call 7bb into 27bb pot — hero getting 27:7 (~3.86:1, needs ~21% equity). Hero is BTN closing action IP. SPR after the call would be ~3.2. Per-villain range chains: CO 3-bettor squeezing vs UTG-open + BTN-imminent range is QQ+/AKs/AKo plus suited blocker bluffs (A5s-A2s, KQs, KJs). On J-7-2 rainbow dry static board CO range-bets at very high frequency with a small size — board entirely favors the 3-bettor's overpair range. Value continues: AA, KK, QQ (overpairs dominating hero), AK with gutter outs and overcards (hero ahead), JJ set (hero blocks 2 combos heavily with AcJs), 77/22 sets rare. Bluff continues: A5s-A2s, KQs/KJs with backdoors. UTG cold-caller of the 3-bet is range-capped — no AA/KK/AK (would 4-bet), leaves JJ-99/QQ-mixed, AQs, sometimes 89s-T9s suited connectors; UTG checked which is consistent with the entire capped range. UTG could check-raise sets/overpairs but flatting JJ-99/AQ behind is more common in 3-bet-pot OOP cold-caller theory. Equity tensions: hero AcJs is top pair top kicker, blocks JJ heavily (2 of 3 remaining J combos), blocks AJ (hero IS AJ); ahead of AK, bluff-blockers, UTG's underpairs/AQ; behind QQ+/set-J. HU-equivalent equity vs CO ~55-58%; 3-way realization ~0.85 dropping to HU when UTG folds turn. Spot factors: hero is closing the flop IP — UTG behind is capped and has already checked, so raise risk from UTG is minimal but exists. RAISE-vs-CALL: raising to ~21bb (3x) folds out CO's entire bluff frequency (the suited-A blockers and KQs/KJs that have no equity vs raise) while continuing only QQ+ and AK that has hero dominated or flipping with worse pot odds. CALL retains CO's bluff range, lets hero realize equity IP cheaply, denies UTG no information (UTG already capped), and matches the calibration anchor on the IDENTICAL board (4WC-3BET-2: AK on Jh7d2s = CALL — AJ is strictly stronger here with a pair). Decision: CALL the 7bb. Adjacent alternatives: RAISE is dominated because it folds out the worse hands hero beats and continues the better hands hero loses to, with no fold equity gain vs CO's value; FOLD is absurd given TPTK + IP + pot odds. Dissent vs Sonnet RAISE majority: Sonnet appears to be overvaluing TPTK in low-SPR 3-bet pot — classic over-aggression error that 4WC-3BET-2 calibrates against.
